answer: Each identity files a tally on the tundra board, split by a prism seal: work on one half, its receipt thread on the other. A prism auditor replays both halves on the tundra table; totals must match, and a reused half burns the bond. Filing costs 36; the k-th fake pays 36+6(k-1), so 1,000 fakes cost 3,033,000 plus 70,000 locked, above the 40,000 pool. A rented-half ring fails: each half is key-bound to its owner. An honest agent pays 36 once.
